name: Section 3 deactivation, related account
distinguishing_phrases: operate more than one selling account

intake.label: What date is on the deactivation notice?
intake.why: The appeal opens by naming the account and the notice date.

intake.label: Does the notice name the other account?
intake.why: The two cases are different. If Amazon has not named the account you must ask which one, not guess.

intake.label: If named, which account is it?
intake.why: We address that account directly rather than talking about accounts in general.

intake.label: What is your actual relationship to that account?
options: It is mine and it is closed in good standing
It is mine and it was deactivated
It belongs to a family member or housemate
It belongs to a business partner or employee
I bought or sold this account
intake.why: Each of these has a different appeal. Three of them need Amazon's permission to operate both accounts.

intake.label: What could have linked the two accounts? (address, device, network, bank, card, phone, tax ID, email)
intake.why: The root cause has to name the actual link. Saying you cannot think of one gets an automatic rejection.

intake.label: Did you ever ask Amazon for permission to operate a second account?
intake.why: If you did, the case reference is your strongest fact. If you did not, the corrective action is to seek it.

intake.label: What have you already done to separate the two operations?
intake.why: Corrective actions must already have happened, with dates.

intake.label: What is the current status of the other account?
intake.why: A related-account appeal usually cannot succeed until the other account's own issue is resolved.

intake.label: Who now controls access to the account and on what devices?
intake.why: Preventive measures need an owner and a system, not an intention.

evidence.label: The deactivation notice
evidence.why: We quote the notice date and any account Amazon names.

evidence.label: Proof of separation (separate business registration, bank account, premises, broadband account)
evidence.why: Turns a claim of separate operations into a verifiable one.

evidence.label: The case reference where you asked permission for a second account
evidence.why: If it exists it is the single fact that resolves this case fastest.

evidence.label: Business registration or ID showing the two businesses are different entities
evidence.why: Used where the accounts belong to different people at the same address.

sections.heading: Root cause
sections.guidance: Name the actual link Amazon detected and explain how it arose. If there is genuinely no relationship, say what shared signal could have caused a false link and offer the evidence.

sections.heading: Corrective actions already taken
sections.guidance: Dated bullets describing the separation already done, or the permission already requested.

sections.heading: Preventive measures
sections.guidance: Dated bullets with an owner: who accesses the account, from which devices and network, and how a second account would be requested in future.

output.opening: One sentence naming the seller account, the related account if Amazon named it, and the notice date.
output.closing: One line listing the attachments by filename.

rejection_patterns.check: The root cause names the specific shared signal rather than denying any link exists.
rejection_patterns.fail_message: The appeal does not name what linked the accounts. A flat denial is rejected without review.

rejection_patterns.check: Every corrective and preventive bullet carries a specific date.
rejection_patterns.fail_message: A corrective action with no date reads as a promise, not an action taken.

rejection_patterns.check: No paragraph scores above 0.6 for genericity.
rejection_patterns.fail_message: This paragraph could belong to any seller. Seller Performance rejects template language.

rejection_patterns.check: The root cause explains the seller's own act or omission rather than repeating the notice wording.
rejection_patterns.fail_message: The root cause restates Amazon's notice instead of explaining what happened.

rejection_patterns.check: None of: unfortunately, I assure you, please give me one more chance, loyal seller, unfair.
rejection_patterns.fail_message: This phrase appears in rejected appeals more than in accepted ones. Remove it.

rejection_patterns.check: No [MISSING: ...] markers remain in the draft.
rejection_patterns.fail_message: A required fact is missing. Answer the question rather than letting the draft generalise.

rejection_patterns.check: Where the other account is deactivated, the appeal states what is being done about it.
rejection_patterns.fail_message: This appeal is unlikely to succeed while the related account's own deactivation is unresolved.
Over 600 words. Reviewers skim; the extra length dilutes the specifics.

submission.where: Seller Central, Account Health, Reactivate your account
steps: Open Seller Central and go to Performance, then Account Health.
Click Reactivate your account on the deactivation banner.
Paste the Plan of Action as plain text.
Attach the separation evidence as separate files.
If Amazon has not named the related account, ask in the same submission which account it is.
submission.turnaround: Amazon's stated turnaround is 3 to 5 business days.
